subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Evaluate ∫ tanⁿx dx, hence evaluate ∫ tan⁵x dx and ∫ tan⁶x dx.

mark_split.label: Set up the split tanⁿx = tanⁿ⁻²x(sec²x − 1)
Integrate by substitution and box the reduction formula

insider_note: This reduction needs no integration by parts at all — tanⁿx splits algebraically into a substitutable piece and a lower power, which is faster to write out under exam time pressure than the by-parts chain used for sinⁿ, cosⁿ, secⁿ and cscⁿ.

steps.label: Set up the split tanⁿx = tanⁿ⁻²x(sec²x − 1)
lines: Let I_n = ∫ tanⁿx dx = ∫ tanⁿ⁻²x · tan²x dx
steps.why: Writing tan²x = sec²x − 1 splits the integral into a piece that is directly substitutable (tanⁿ⁻²x sec²x, since sec²x is the derivative of tanx) and a lower power of tanx.
common_mistakes: Trying integration by parts here instead — it works for sinⁿ, cosⁿ, secⁿ, cscⁿ but is the slow route for tanⁿ.
Writing tan²x = 1 − sec²x with the sign flipped.
steps.memory_tip: tan²x = sec²x − 1 is the identity that turns tanⁿx into something you can substitute.

steps.label: Integrate by substitution and box the reduction formula
lines: In the first integral put t = tanx ⇒ dt = sec²x dx
∫ tanⁿ⁻²x sec²x dx = ∫ tⁿ⁻²dt = tⁿ⁻¹/(n−1) = tanⁿ⁻¹x/(n−1)
steps.why: The substitution t = tanx turns ∫tanⁿ⁻²x sec²x dx into a plain power rule in t, giving the tanⁿ⁻¹x/(n−1) term directly — no by-parts needed anywhere in this reduction.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to convert back from t to tanx after integrating tⁿ⁻².
Writing the power as n instead of n−1 in the exponent after integrating.
steps.memory_tip: Power rule in t, then swap t back for tanx — one substitution does the whole job.

steps.label: Evaluate ∫ tan⁵x dx
lines: I₃ = tan²x/2 − I₁, and I₁ = ∫tanx dx = log|secx| + c

lines.text: ∴ ∫ tan⁵x dx = tan⁴x/4 − tan²x/2 + log|secx| + c

steps.why: Odd n chains down through I₃ to I₁ = ∫tanx dx, the ONE tanⁿ integral that is not itself a power — it is the standard log|secx| result, so the chain stops there.
common_mistakes: Chaining down to I₀ = x by mistake, which is the even-n stopping point, not the odd-n one.
Dropping the modulus bars on log|secx|, which makes the antiderivative undefined wherever secx < 0.
steps.memory_tip: Odd n stops at I₁ = log|secx|; even n stops at I₀ = x — never mix the two chains up.

steps.label: Evaluate ∫ tan⁶x dx
lines: I₆ = tan⁵x/5 − I₄, I₄ = tan³x/3 − I₂, I₂ = tanx − I₀, and I₀ = ∫dx = x
So I₂ = tanx − x, I₄ = tan³x/3 − tanx + x

lines.text: ∴ ∫ tan⁶x dx = tan⁵x/5 − tan³x/3 + tanx − x + c

steps.why: Even n chains down through I₄ and I₂ to I₀ = x — the same even-n chain as sinⁿ and cosⁿ, just with tanx's own reduction formula doing the stepping down.
common_mistakes: Reusing the odd-n answer for tan⁵x by mistake instead of working the even-n chain fresh.
Sign slip when substituting I₂ = tanx − x back into the I₄ line.
steps.memory_tip: Work the chain n → n−2 → … ALL the way to I₀ or I₁ before writing the boxed answer — never stop one step early.
